thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: control-plane - elevated 5xx rate detected for /v1/org/* and /v1/auth/* (90m window). P50 latency up 3x. Paging oncall. :rotating_light:
Alice (oncall): saw the bot, I'm oncall — will gather initial triage. Can someone grab impact? :hand:
Emma (support): getting multiple customer reports: two enterprise customers seeing API errors in the last 10m, support ticket numbers #9874 and #9875. Error seen: 502 Gateway.
Ben (sre): I'm up. Pulling logs and metrics now. Do we have any recent deploys to control-plane services?
Devon (controlplane): no deploys in last 2 hours from control-plane team. Noted a config rollout earlier to 3 replicas for config-service ~1h ago (automated).
Carla (auth): I'm seeing auth-service spike in connection errors to auth-db pool around 12:03 UTC — many retries. Error snippet from auth logs: ```
2026-03-15T12:03:21Z ERROR auth-db/query timeout after 1500ms conn_id=0x7f9e1
2026-03-15T12:03:22Z WARN auth-service request_id=abcd1234 upstream=org-lookup 504
```
Ben (sre): metrics: org-lookup and billing downstreams showing timeouts ~12:02-12:05. Control-plane 5xx rate increased from 0.4% -> 8% in 5m. Likely a dependency cascade.
Alice (oncall): severity? Customer-impacting multiple customers -> sev2. Paging SRE. @Ben please own mitigation, @Carla and @Devon assist for auth/org lookup.
Ben (sre): starting runbook: 1) confirm whether circuit-breakers tripped; 2) check DB replica health; 3) enable degraded-mode routing; 4) add retry/jitter adjustments. Running queries on service registry now.
Ben (sre): checking gateway traces: many requests failing with upstream error code 502 from auth-proxy -> org-lookup. Sample trace ID: trace-0ef9. Command I'm running: `curl -sS http://metrics.internal/controlplane/trace/trace-0ef9 | jq .`
Devon (controlplane): org-lookup's host count dropped — autoscaler scaled down a pod group due to failed liveness probes (OOMKilled) around 11:58. New pods failing liveness -> cascading 502 from auth-service when calling org-lookup.
Carla (auth): auth has fallback cache, but it's disabled by strict validation flag. Suggest enabling fallback cache for 15m to reduce upstream calls. If we flip the flag, auth will serve slightly stale org metadata for reads. Need approval.
Alice (oncall): approve fallback cache for 15m. Post a note when done.
Carla (auth): flipping flag now: `kubectl -n controlplane set env deployment/auth-service ENABLE_FALLBACK_CACHE=true --record`
Ops-bot: deploy event recorded by ops-bot: auth-service env update applied to 2/2 pods.
Carla (auth): cache enabled, warming now. Cache hit rate currently 2% -> 40% (warming).
Ben (sre): seeing 5xx rate drop to 3.1% within 60s. Latency p50 back to 1.6x baseline. Good sign.
Emma (support): reporting back to affected customers that we're investigating and applying mitigation; will update again in 15m.
Devon (controlplane): investigating root cause for org-lookup OOMs. Finding a GC/heap growth regression in latest image; pods had increased RSS before OOM. I recommend reverting the config-service rollout (the one that touched memory limits) to avoid further pressure on shared DB replicas.
Ben (sre): while Devon reverts, I'm opening temporary circuit-breaker on gateway for org-lookup calls to fail fast after 200ms and route to fallback flow. Patch to proxy config: ```
- upstream_timeout: 1200ms
+ upstream_timeout: 200ms
+ use_local_fallback: true
``` Applying to canary gateway group.
Ops-bot: gateway config applied to canary (gw-canary-2). Monitoring.
Ben (sre): canary shows requests succeed with fallback; overall 5xx now 1.8%.
Devon (controlplane): rolling back config-service rollout to previous image: `kubectl -n controlplane rollout undo deployment/config-service` — started.
Carla (auth): auth-db connection count is stabilizing. No new connection errors after cache and gateway fallback.
Alice (oncall): timeline so far: 11:58 autoscaler OOM kill -> 12:02 spikes starts -> 12:05 fallback cache enabled -> 12:10 gateway fallback and config rollback started -> system stabilizing 12:12-12:15.
Ben (sre): creating mitigation checklist and capturing commands in incident doc. We should also consider increasing memory limits and temporary DB connection pool increase for org-lookup. Devon, can you create a remediation PR?
Devon (controlplane): yes I'll open PR to bump memory and add a liveness probe tweak to reduce false OOMs. PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/controlplane/PR-4212
Emma (support): customers updated: both enterprise tickets moved to 'Mitigation in progress', next ETA update in 30m. No new SEV reports.
Alice (oncall): handoff: Ben, are you staying on to finish remediation or should I hand to night oncall at 13:00?
Ben (sre): I'll stay for next 45m to validate remediation and confirm rollback health. If stable, I'll create a follow-up ticket for postmortem and handoff to next oncall at 13:00.
Carla (auth): note for postmortem: enable telemetry around cache fallback usage, record decision and impact; ensure cache TTLs documented for fallback mode.
Ops-bot: Incident ticket created: INC-2026-337 control-plane dependency cascade -> elevated 5xx. Severity: SEV2. Link: https://incidents.redwood/INC-2026-337
Ben (sre): adding immediate action items to ticket: (a) revert config rollout (done), (b) increase memory for org-lookup (PR opened), (c) tune liveness probes, (d) add safety circuit to gateway config for org-lookup.
Alice (oncall): last check before brief handoff: 5xx rate at 0.9%, error traces decreasing, no new customer escalations. I'm marking this thread as 'monitoring' and will hand to Ben at 13:00 for formal postmortem assignment.
Emma (support): I'll follow up with customers and update status pages: we should note degraded reads were possible and we've enabled cached fallback to restore availability.
Devon (controlplane): rollback completed on all replicas. Services back to previous image as of 12:18.
Carla (auth): confirming GC tuning and connection pool plan in PR https://git.internal/r/redwood/auth/PR-998
Ben (sre): thanks team. Leaving a short runbook note in pagerduty: "If auth->org-lookup 5xx spike: enable fallback cache, apply gateway short-timeout fallback, consider rollback to previous config-image."
Alice (oncall): handing to Ben (sre) at 13:00 UTC. If anything spikes before then, escalate to @Devon and @Carla.
Ben (sre): acknowledged. I'll run a 30m watch and then file postmortem. Closing active mitigation phase.
incident-bot: NOTE: This thread will be archived. Please attach logs and any follow-up actions to INC-2026-337 for the postmortem.
